Checked. This paper's route 1 (new DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay, area commutative, accepted) carries big-cm-fixed, big-cm-balanced (Definition 4.1.1(1)–(2), p. 84) and direct-summand. PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23's route 10 (part-ii of SchemeAndStackFoundations, accepted five minutes later) carries big-cm and balanced-cm for arbitrary modules (§2.2(b)–(c), with no finite-generation hypothesis) and splinter (Definition 2.12), and its brief says 'Build big/balanced/cohomological CM predicates'. For a Noetherian regular (hence reduced) R, a finite injective R → S makes S a faithful finite R-module, so the direct summand theorem is exactly 'regular rings are splinters'. The predicates are therefore planned twice, and the module form is the more general. PAPER-BHATT-18's accepted route 9 has the same kind, id, title and area as route 1, so it coalesces and adds no third copy. One detail of the claim is inaccurate: there are cross-references between the two extractions (BHATT-ETAL-23 screens the companion's ramification Part II, and this file cites BHATT-ETAL-23 for the Matlis supplier), but none on these predicates. Medium is right.
The direction of the fix is right and acyclic. DirectSummands' early layers import only R03.1, R03.3, DD.1 and pinned regular sequences, nothing from the Scheme Part II, so that Part II can import an early DirectSummands layer. Two adjustments:
- (a) 'Mark /big-cm, /balanced-cm and /splinter as imports' has no protocol meaning, since a missing item is routed exactly once. In PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23, move those three items to a route of kind 'new' with the same roadmap id, title and area as this route 1, so that the three extractions coalesce. Route 10's brief keeps its consumers (closure vanishing, BCM test ideals, B⁰) and imports the predicates.
- (b) In this route 1's brief, state the predicates for arbitrary modules (BHATT-ETAL-23 §2.2's weakly regular form) in the first layer, before the perfectoid-dependent layers, derive André's algebra forms 4.1.1(1)–(2) from them, and add 'every Noetherian regular ring is a splinter' to direct-summand.
Since #3361 and #3479 are open, the maintainer should know.

Checked. p. 75: 'Le cas où B contient un corps étant déjà connu, c'est le cas où B est d'inégale caractéristique (0, p) (sans p-torsion) que nous traitons.' §4.3, p. 87: 'D'après le th. 0.7.1 (et [17] en égale caractéristique), il existe une S_{m,i}-algèbre de Cohen-Macaulay T_{m,i}'. Theorem 0.7.1 is stated for every Noetherian local ring, so the published theorem rests on the equal-characteristic existence of balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebras directly, and inside the reduction to a p-torsion-free domain, since passing to B/P for a minimal prime P of maximal dimension can land in characteristic p. The extraction's own notes say so (big-cm-existence: 'the equal-characteristic case is Hochster's and is a prerequisite'), no item states it, and the only prerequisite covering it, Hochster–Huneke 1995, is marked 'Not read'. For (b), unramified-reduction's proof says 'Equal-characteristic cases are separate known inputs', while frobenius-direct-summand-char-p and invertible-degree-retraction are depended on by nothing on this path. Medium is right.
Three corrections to the fix:
- (1) The 1992 title is wrong. Crossref gives M. Hochster and C. Huneke, 'Infinite integral extensions and big Cohen–Macaulay algebras', Ann. of Math. 135 (1992) 53–89, doi:10.2307/2946563; its theorem is that R⁺ is balanced big CM for an excellent local domain of characteristic p, and equal characteristic 0 comes from the reduction in Hochster–Huneke 1995.
- (2) The example B = Z_p[[x]]/(px) also has the mixed-characteristic choice P = (x). B = Z_p[[x, y]]/(px, py) is sharper: its only minimal prime of maximal dimension is (p), of characteristic p, so the equal-characteristic case is needed inside the mixed-characteristic proof, not merely available.
- (3) The characteristic-p half is also stated by the accepted PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23/plus-completion-cm (for an excellent local domain of residue characteristic p, the p-adic completion of R⁺ is balanced big CM). The new item should name it, and the single owner of finding 3 should take both.
Also put frobenius-direct-summand-char-p and invertible-degree-retraction in the dependencies of unramified-reduction, whose conclusion covers all Noetherian regular rings, rather than of direct-summand.

Checked on the p. 81 page image and against §1.2 (pp. 76–77) and §§2.2–2.4. Step (a) reads '(a) A_j0⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩{f_ik/ϖ_ik} est plate sur A_j0 ; or, le spectre analytique de A_j0 est réunion croissante des polydisques affinoïdes de rayons r ∈ |K°°_∞|, et pour une telle algèbre de Tate B_r, B_r⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩{f_ik/ϖ_ik} est même plate sur B_r⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩ [3, prop. 2.2.4]'. A_j0 = A°_j0[1/p] is not affinoid, and the passage from each B_r to A_j0 would need A_j0 → B_r flat and a base-change identification that is not automatic for a module not finite over A_j0. So the printed sentence is a sketch whose key step is unjustified, rather than 'no argument'.
The repair checks out step by step:
- (i) C = A°_j0⟨T^{1/p^j}, U⟩/(ϖ_ik U − f_ik) is ϖ_j-torsion-free. §1.2.1's coefficient argument uses only that multiplication by f_ik is isometric, and A_j0⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩ is multiplicatively normed (§2.4) with |f_ik| = 1 by step (b); the paper relies on the same fact for (17).
- (ii) C is Noetherian and ϖ_j-adically complete.
- (iii) C/ϖ_j is free over A°_j0/ϖ_j by (b).
- (iv) With ϖ_j a non-zero-divisor, Tor_1^{A/ϖ^n}(A/ϖ, C/ϖ^n) = ker(ϖ)/ϖ^{n−1}(C/ϖ^n) = 0 by torsion-freeness, so each C/ϖ_j^n is flat over A°_j0/ϖ_j^n by the criterion over a nilpotent ideal.
- (v) Stacks Lemma 15.28.4 (tag 0912) then makes C = lim C/ϖ_j^n flat over A°_j0, which is the conclusion the paragraph draws, and (a) follows by inverting p.
So the statement of (a) is true, and 'gap, affects nothing' and low are right. The fix is right, with the reason reworded as above and the adapter keeping the hypothesis that ϖ is a non-zero-divisor on the Noetherian ring. generic-fibre-flat, flatness-by-fibres and affinoid-rational-flat have no other consumers, so they may be deleted, or generic-fibre-flat kept as a corollary recording the printed route.

Checked on the page images of pp. 78 and 82. §2.2: 'On permet la valeur ∞ pour l'un des indices (ou les deux), en prenant la réunion indexée par les valeurs finies de cet indice.' Corollaire 2.6.1: 'Pour tout (j, k), A°_j0 ↪ A°_jk est pur. Démonstration. — Il suffit de montrer que A°_∞∞ est pur sur A°_∞0, puisque ce dernier est pur sur chaque A°_j0.' kummer-finite-purity says 'For every finite pair (j,k)', dropping the infinite-index cases, including (∞, ∞), which is what the proof proves. The deduction covers all j, k ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}: A°_j0 → A°_∞0 is faithfully flat (§2.3), hence pure; A°_∞0 → A°_∞∞ is pure by the proof; the composite is pure; and each A°_j0 → A°_jk is a left factor of it. Low is right, and the fix is right. The added dependencies pure-composition and pure-left-factor sit on route 1 while the item is on route 4, which is acyclic as long as they are in route 1's early purity prefix, as the briefs require. Also add coordinate-tower-flat (§2.3) as the input of the faithful-flatness step.
